title: Python SDK: ergonomics for streaming chat completions, event callbacks, and retry-safety helpers
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Create a clean, developer-friendly Python streaming chat API surface that makes it easy to consume token-by-token output, handle structured events (function calls, deltas, metadata), and safely retry or resume failed streams without duplicating side effects. Deliverables: a public API proposal, reference examples, compatibility shims for existing SDK users, unit + integration tests, and docs page with curation of common patterns (callbacks, async iterators, buffered retries).
proposal: We will expose three first-class ergonomics for streaming chat completions: (1) async iterator 'stream_chat' that yields ChatStreamEvent objects, (2) callback registration via 'on_event' with typed callbacks for {token, delta, function_start, function_append, function_end, done, error, metadata}, and (3) a 'safe_stream' helper/context manager that provides an at-most-once emission guarantee for downstream consumers when retries happen. Implementation details: - Server-side will attach monotonically increasing 'event_index' to every event to support idempotent replay. - SDK will buffer a short tail of emitted events (configurable, default 64 tokens) in memory to de-duplicate on retry. - For cases with side effects (webhooks, DB writes), recommend the customer provide an idempotency key per request; SDK will surface that param. - Backwards compatibility: existing blocking streaming function name 'chat_stream' becomes a thin shim over the new primitives. - Expose a simple 'resume_token' from the server if available; SDK uses it to request a resume slice. If resume is not supported, SDK falls back to the buffered-de-dup approach.
design_notes: Event model: flatten to single event stream with 'type' field; avoid nested payloads to make iteration cheap.
Each event includes: type, text (optional), name (for function calls), event_index (int), metadata (map serialized as JSON string).
Backpressure: SDK will surface a 'max_queue_size' parameter for callback path to avoid unbounded memory growth with slow consumers.
Retries: use exponential backoff with jitter. For resumed streams, request 'from_index' if supported by server. Otherwise re-open and de-duplicate via buffered tail.
Testing: add integration tests that inject transient connection drops at random offsets and assert no duplicated application-visible events when using safe_stream.
Telemetry: emit metrics for 'resume_supported', 'retry_count', 'deduped_events' to aid debugging and product decisions.
Docs: add cookbook entries: 'displaying typing indicator', 'function call streaming', 'resilient streaming for webhooks'.
acceptance_criteria: Public API implemented: stream_chat (async iterator), stream_chat_with_callbacks (callback map), safe_stream context manager.
Unit tests covering event shapes, ordering, and callback dispatching.
Integration tests simulating transient disconnects prove at-most-once delivery for safe_stream when idempotency key is provided.
Examples added in repo under examples/python/streaming/ demonstrating token-by-token UI, function_call streaming, and retry-safe writes to sqlite.
Docs page published and approved by developer experience lead (link in attachments).
